text:
rachel_finance: Heads-up — BlueFjord (acct BF-332) invoice INV-2026-0912 charged full amount; promo BFSPRING2026 didn't apply. customer paid $11,200; expected after promo = $9,200. requesting $2,000 promo credit plus $200 goodwill. can we do a $2,200 refund?

tom_billing: please paste the invoice period + simple math snippet for the JE. also want to know if it's already reconciled in AR.

rachel_finance: invoice period: Feb 2026. calc: `subtotal = 10,000; usage tax = 1,200; gross = 11,200; promo_expected = -2,000; net_expected = 9,200; discrepancy = 2,000; goodwill = 200; total_refund = 2,200`

lia_support: BlueFjord opened support ticket #BF-4587 on 2026-03-10 asking why promo not applied. they escalated to account team.

nate_sales: they paid on 2026-03-12 via ACH. want refund to original payment method. they've indicated it's impacting their cash forecast.

eric_eng: quick root cause: promo lookup failed due to case-sensitivity change in the promo service deployment on 2026-03-09. fixed in canary; will roll to prod today. logs attached (link).

rachel_finance: because payment cleared, requesting refund RFD-99001 for $2,200. GL guidance?

oliver_fd: approved. use GL 4020 (Promo Liability) for the $2,000 and GL 4075 (Customer Goodwill) for the $200. JE ref = JE-2026-0500. please include memo "BlueFjord promo misapply + goodwill".

tom_billing: next steps I will take: 1) create refund RFD-99001 for $2,200 scheduled 2026-03-23 to original ACH, 2) post JE-2026-0500, 3) update INV-2026-0912 status to refunded, 4) send confirmation to customer.

billing-bot: Refund RFD-99001 created by tom_billing for $2,200, payout scheduled 2026-03-23. internal ref PAY-3399.

lia_support: i'll draft the customer message and cc @nate_sales. keep it clear this was a system error; offer the goodwill note.

rachel_finance: i'll mark the AR entry for reconciliation once the payout posts and exclude this event from usage SLA reports. closing the loop on my side.

tom_billing: invoice and refund updated. will ping when payout clears.
